findings.finding: Line 16 is blank, so the table ends after the I07-4 row. Lines 17-19 hold the SEC-4, HI-7 and SEC-QW4 rows, but they have no header or delimiter row of their own. GitHub-flavoured Markdown therefore renders them as one paragraph with literal pipes, not as table rows. These three rows are the main change of this round.
findings.requiredChange: Delete the blank line 16 so that the five rows form one table under the 'Text, ownership or share' header.

findings.finding: The scope decision reads 'add SEC-4 and HI-7 (+HE-003 call site, +HE-008 uid, unit start state and SELinux self-permissions)'. The proposal it approves, HE-002S design §4, says 'SEC-4 and HI-7 add HE-003 (...) and HE-008 (uid, unit start state, SELinux permissions)'. HI-7 already lists HE-008, so for HI-7 the HE-008 addition is a share only. SEC-4's plan v2 packets are HE-002S and HE-004..HE-007, without HE-008, and the amendment does not add it: packetsAdded is [HE-003] and there is no HE-008 share. Neither the record nor the README says that HE-008 was left out of SEC-4, or why. The omission can be argued on substance: SEC-4 is 'Install exactly the compiled programs', while HE-008's share covers uid, start state and SELinux. Against that, the start state and planeon_gate_t's setpcap and setcap permissions are preconditions for the seal to reach its install step (design §2). Either way, the record applies an unstated reading of an owner decision.
findings.requiredChange: Choose one of two fixes. (1) Add HE-008 to SEC-4 as the decision and design §4 read: packetsAdded [HE-003, HE-008], packets [HE-002S, HE-003, HE-004, HE-005, HE-006, HE-007, HE-008], and HE-008's EFFECT_GATE share. (2) State in SEC-4's change and in the README that HE-008's share is recorded under HI-7 only, give the reason, and confirm that reading with the owner via the lane monitor before adoption.

findings.finding: HE-003's share says that main 'calls stage 2' but does not say what HE-003 passes to stage 2. Design §2 makes `kept` an input from HE-003: 'CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE exactly when the signed I04 port is below 1024, else nothing. The configuration format and its I04 port are HE-003's ... HE-002S's API takes `kept` as a value'. B1 says the same: '`kept` is a value HE-003's configuration supplies'. This is the only conditional item in EFFECT_GATE's HI-7 row (HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md:405: 'None, except CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE if the signed I04 port is below 1024'). No plan v2 obligation names an owner for deriving it: no obligation mentions the I04 port or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE. As the share is written, an HE-003 that always passes CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE would satisfy it. A second, smaller gap would be a NOTE on its own: HE-008's share says 'uid 0', but the seal's precondition is uid 0 and gid 0 (design §2: getresuid and getresgid, all three ids 0), and the unit sets both.
findings.requiredChange: In HE-003's share for SEC-4 and HI-7, and in the README rows, state that HE-003 derives `kept` from the signed configuration's I04 port and passes it to stage 2 (design §2, B1). `kept` is CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE exactly when that port is below 1024, else empty. In HE-008's share, write 'uid 0 and gid 0'. Both changes fall within the scope decision's '+HE-003 call site' and '+HE-008 uid', so no new owner decision is needed.

findings.finding: The record does not define what a `shares` entry means for a packet that plan v2 already lists. For HE-003, which is newly added, the share is its whole part. HE-008 is already in HI-7 for every role (units, SELinux modules), and its share 'for EFFECT_GATE: ...' is meant as an addition: the decision says '+HE-008'. On its own, though, a share could be read as the packet's whole part of the obligation, in the way I07-4's `ownership` is HE-002B's whole part. That reading would narrow HE-008's HI-7 part to EFFECT_GATE. Separately, PACKETS_ADDED leaves each obligation's text as plan v2 has it. SEC-QW4 therefore still reads 'steady state is W02d v3 and T04', next to HE-002S's steady-state share.
findings.requiredChange: State in the README, and in the mechanics layer's schema check, three rules: a share is what the named packet owns for this change, in addition to its plan v2 part; a listed packet without a share keeps its plan v2 part; and the obligation's text is unchanged.

findings.finding: The three new changes cite 'HE-002S design revision 2 (B6)' and '(B4, B6)'. The HE-003 shares cite owner decisions Q-HE2S-4 (a) and Q-HE2S-5 (a). The design is an operator-side document, and B4 and B6 are its review-disposition ids, not repository lines. Q-HE2S-4 and Q-HE2S-5 appear in no repository file except in these citations (grep of the subject). By contrast, this packet carries Q-HE2S-1, Q-HE2S-2, Q-HE2S-3, Q-HE2B-2, A13 and the scope decision verbatim. The citation '(owner decision Q-HE2S-4 (a))' also follows 'exits with a distinct status on any seal error', which comes from design §2 and §6 (B6), not from Q-HE2S-4. The share texts themselves are faithful to the design: I compared them with §2, §4, §6, §12 and §14.
findings.requiredChange: Either carry Q-HE2S-4 (a) and Q-HE2S-5 (a) verbatim in ownerDecisions, as Q-HE2S-3 is carried, or drop the two citations. Say where the design becomes public: design §6 says the HE-003 carry is recorded in the HE-002S PR. Cite its sections (§2, §6) as well as the B-ids. Put the Q-HE2S-4 citation directly after the two-stage clause.
